class.name: NetwServerInfo
class.brief_description: The server metadata an [code]NPRB[/code] probe reply carries.
class.description:
A probe asks a host what it is without joining it, and this is the answer: the fields a browser row needs to decide whether to connect at all. It is a plain record with a codec, so the same object crosses the wire and fills a list entry. A session with no declared provider answers with [method from_session]. A game that wants more declares one through [method Netw.configure_server_info], and is handed that same base record to edit rather than an API to read. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_server_info(self, server_info)
func server_info(info: NetwServerInfo) -> NetwServerInfo: info.motd = "Ranked, no friendly fire" info.game_mode = &"ranked" return info [/codeblock] Returning [code]null[/code] or anything that is not a [NetwServerInfo] is a defect rather than a request for the default: the probe answers [constant NetwAuthProtocol.PROBE_ERROR], so a browser row reads a broken host as broken instead of as an empty one. [member metadata] is the open field: anything a game wants a browser to read that the named fields do not carry, encoded and decoded with the rest of the record.

method.name: from_payload
method.description: Decodes [param bytes] into a fresh record, or [code]null[/code] when [param bytes] is empty or does not carry one.

method.name: from_session
method.description: The default probe reply: a copy of [member NetwSessionConfig.server_info] with the live fields overlaid, which are the connected participant count as [member players] and [member NetwSessionConfig.app_id]. [member is_local_listener] is marked, so a caller can tell a live local host from a closed port. The declaration is copied rather than answered, so replying to a probe can never write back into what the game authored. This is what a probe answers with when no [method Netw.configure_server_info] declaration governs the session, and it is also the record a declared provider is handed.

method.name: to_payload
method.description: Serializes [param info] to the probe wire format, or an empty array when [param info] is [code]null[/code].

members.member: The application tag the host gates joins on, so a browser can hide a host running a different game or a different build.
The mode the host is running, as the game names it. Unset by the built-in provider.
Whether this record was built by a live host rather than assembled from a directory listing. A browser reads it to tell a host that answered from one it only heard about.
The round trip [method NetwMultiplayer.endpoint_probe] measured reaching this host, in milliseconds. [code]-1[/code] means unmeasured, which is what a row assembled from a listing carries.
The cap the host advertises. Advisory: the host's own admission decides.
Free-form fields a game adds to the reply. Carried through the codec untouched.
The message the host shows in a browser row. Unset by the built-in provider.
The live participant count at the moment the reply was built.
The build string the game publishes. Unset by the built-in provider.

How widely the host asked to be listed, as a [enum Visibility]. What a directory does with anything but [constant VISIBILITY_PUBLIC] belongs to that directory: this says what the host asked for, not what any service enforces.

constants.constant: Listed only to players the host's platform calls friends. A directory with no such notion treats it as [constant VISIBILITY_PRIVATE].
Not listed at all. The host is still joinable by anyone holding its address.
